title: Sensitivity audit logbook: finance queries & calibration notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a running internal review log for the Optimize cost model calibration work. Focus is on the data sources we used, the calibration steps we ran against actual hosted usage, outstanding finance questions for sign-off, and a prioritized list of changes to the working spreadsheets. Treat as a working notebook — expect short, incremental updates.

Status summary (short):
- Model baseline: v3.1 (spreadsheet: /d/1a2b3c-optimize-cost-model, tab: SUMMARY-v3)
- Last reconciliation run: 2025-02-28 (matched ~86% of invoice-level spend categories to model line-items)
- Main open items: GPU amortization methodology, network egress treatment for cross-region, and tokenization inefficiency multiplier for chat workloads.

1) Data sources we used (notes & caveats):
- Hosted billing invoices (raw): Finance S3 export for 2024 Q4 to 2025 Q1. Caveat: tagging inconsistent for burst capacity — see invoice rows flagged with "unclassified-burst".
- Telemetry sampling: request traces sampled 1:50 for token-level latency/seq_len distribution (prod region us-west1). Caveat: sample underrepresents long-tail enterprise routes.
- Dedicated usage reports: internal dashboard exports (daily GPU-hr by customer) from Dedicated v1.2. Caveat: some days include maintenance windows that inflate avg utilization — see maintenance-notes tab.
- Model perf benchmarks: per-model token-per-second and memory footprints from infra/team-benchmarks/mb-2024-12. Caveat: bench runs use 1k context synthetic prompts; real user contexts skew shorter/longer depending on app.
- Storage & KV cache costs: S3 and Redis cost lines mapped from infra billing export. Caveat: ephemeral KV replica counts vary by deployment; we used median across customers.

2) Calibration procedure (what we did):
- Step A: Mapped invoice categories -> model cost buckets. Manual override mapping for 9 categories. Rationale: bundle costs (support, platform-subscriptions) are being allocated as a fixed overhead; flagged for product decision.
- Step B: Replayed sampled traces through the model-profile table to estimate tokens generated vs tokens billed. Applied a tokenization inefficiency multiplier of 1.07 (initial estimate).
- Step C: Matched observed GPU-hr from dedicated exports to model throughput to infer real-world tokens/hr per GPU for each model family.
- Step D: Applied an availability overhead of 1.12x to baseline GPU costs to account for autoscaling headroom and failed-schedule buffers (derived from SRE incident windows Q4).
- Step E: Ran sensitivity Monte Carlo (n=10k) across three axes: seq_len, batch efficiency (0.6–0.95), and KV cache hit-rate (0.2–0.9). Observed unit-cost median variation ~+/-18%, tail up to +60% with low batching and low cache.

3) Key calibration outcomes (numbers to call out):
- Baseline per-1k token cost (hosted, averaged across models): $0.0041/token (converted to per-token unit for UX simplicity).
- Dedicated marginal GPU-hour cost after overheads (amortized capex + infra + ops): $6.40/GPU-hr (this is intentionally conservative; finance suggests a lower bound of ~$5.20 depending on capex schedule).
- Network egress assumed: $0.08/GB for cross-region; internal notes show negotiated cloud discount could reduce this to $0.045/GB for committed customers.
- Tokenization inefficiency multiplier: 1.07 (orig) — sensitivity suggests range 1.02–1.15 depending on conservative tokenization and escaped output.

4) Open finance questions (require explicit sign-off):
- Q1: GPU amortization window and salvage assumptions. Our amortization uses 36 months linear with 10% salvage. Finance preferred 48 months; decision materially changes dedicated unit cost by ~12%. Action: finance to confirm preferred window by 2025-03-07.
- Q2: Treatment of platform/support fees. Current model allocates them as "platform overhead" spread across all customers equally. Finance prefers top-line allocation by revenue band (tiered). Need direction from PM and Revenue Ops by 2025-03-10.
- Q3: Network egress discounts. We used published list prices. Sales/Partnerships report negotiated discounts; need consolidated discount table (sales to provide by 2025-03-05).

5) Proposed conservative adjustments (recommendations for next draft):
- Adopt finance-amortization-window=48 months for the public working scenario and keep 36 months for an "aggressive efficiency" scenario. Mark both in the spreadsheet and name tabs explicitly.
- Add a new model parameter: "billing-tagging-loss" representing cost leakage where burst capacity isn't tagged (default 1.04 multiplier).
- Introduce a per-route tokenization audit sample for 5 high-volume customers to refine the inefficiency multiplier. Timeline: 3 weeks.

6) Action items & owners (short):
- Priya: merge finance amortization scenarios into SUMMARY-v4 (due 2025-03-06).
- Jonah: request detailed network discount matrix from Sales and drop into linked sheet (JIRA-OPT-547) (due 2025-03-05).
- Lena: run targeted replay on 5 high-volume routes to measure real tokenization inefficiency and send results (due 2025-03-28).
- Marcus: adjust Monte Carlo to include two additional axes: support load (0.8–1.2x) and ingress/de-duplication overhead (0.95–1.1x). Re-run sensitivity and post results (due 2025-03-12).
- Rafael (Finance): confirm amortization window and platform allocation method (due 2025-03-07).

7) Risks & notes for reviewers:
- If finance chooses 48-month amortization plus tiered overhead allocation, hosted per-1k token cost could drop ~9% but Dedicated effective margin expansion will be impacted. Communicate externally only after product has accepted metrics.
- Batch efficiency assumptions have the largest lever on unit cost; small changes in average batch size for streaming chat routes can swing costs significantly. Need engineering guidance on realistic batching for streaming.
- Shadow customers / feature flags: some customers are on experimental routing that increases egress or duplicates requests; those should be excluded from baseline until routing stabilizes.

Appendix — quick reconciliation notes (traceable rows):
- Invoice row sample: INV-2025-01-2345 maps to spreadsheet row: HOSTED_INFRA line 12 (unclassified-burst flagged).
- Dedicated daily export sample: DED-2025-02-10-tenant-42 GPU-hrs=224 mapped to model-family M-3-large throughput estimate 18k tokens/sec (bench) -> used to infer 14.9M tokens/hr effective in production.
- Monte Carlo seed/report: monte-seed-20250228.csv (results tab attached in sheet).

If you're reviewing: please add inline comments in the sheet (referenced above) and flag any finance decisions you think we should hold as product-ops blockers. I'll incorporate finance answers into a v4 that explicitly shows two scenarios (Conservative / Target) and a short one-pager we can give to Sales for pricing conversations.

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep the "platform overhead" visible as both a % and absolute $ per token in the SUMMARY tab.
- Add a TODO to instrument KV replica counts per-customer for a full month to replace median assumption.
- Consider a separate tab for "enterprise routing tax" which models additional egress and tail-latency-induced replication costs.

Last updated 2025-03-04 by Priya Natarajan (prod-optimize).
